title: Linux NUMA Allocation-Miss Ratio
exclusions: Measures deltas of the Linux kernel's normal-page NUMA allocation-policy counters for nodes exposed under `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/numastat`. It does not measure memory-access latency, bandwidth, cache misses, current page placement, per-process locality, or huge-page allocation; prove application impact or root cause; cover hosts without qualified NUMA nodes; or provide regulatory assurance. Kernel documentation warns that memoryless nodes can skew these counters, so such topologies require separate engineering qualification before paging. The base report labels active exact-host-and-node exceptions but does not remove their rows.
evidence: When deployed, retain the `linux_numa_allocation_miss_ratio` saved-report definition, `linux_numa_allocation_miss_alert` alert definition and scheduler history, raw `linux:numa_node_stats` events for the incident interval, the applicable exception-lookup revision, and exported result rows containing `_time`, `host`, `numa_node`, `numa_hit_pages`, `numa_miss_pages`, `hit_miss_pages`, `miss_pct`, `valid_intervals`, `covered_seconds`, and `disposition`. These artifacts show collection and search behavior; they do not claim runtime validation, performance impact, root cause, or compliance.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a temporary index, create nine one-minute-apart events ending one minute before dispatch for `host=numa-positive`, `numa_node=0`, one fixed valid `boot_id`, and `sourcetype=linux:numa_node_stats`. Start at `numa_hit=100000 numa_miss=1000 numa_foreign=1000 local_node=100000 other_node=1000`; for each of eight subsequent events add 900 to `numa_hit`, 100 to `numa_miss`, zero to `numa_foreign`, 900 to `local_node`, and 100 to `other_node`. Run the SPL with the temporary index substituted. Expect exactly one row with `valid_intervals=8`, `covered_seconds=480`, `numa_hit_pages=7200`, `numa_miss_pages=800`, `hit_miss_pages=8000`, `miss_pct=10.0`, and `disposition=investigate`. An unexpired exact `host,numa_node` lookup row must retain the base-report row as `approved_test`; the alert variant ending in `| where disposition="investigate"` must return zero rows.
controlTest.negativeScenario: In the same temporary index, create nine one-minute-apart events for `host=numa-negative`, `numa_node=1`, and one fixed valid `boot_id`. Start all five counters at the positive fixture's initial values, then add 951 to `numa_hit`, 49 to `numa_miss`, zero to `numa_foreign`, 951 to `local_node`, and 49 to `other_node` on each of eight intervals. Expect zero rows because 392 misses out of 8,000 hit-plus-miss page increments is 4.9%, below the inclusive 10% threshold. Separately change the boot ID on the fifth event or decrease a counter; expect the invalid transition to be discarded and fewer than eight valid intervals, therefore zero rows rather than a reset-induced alert.

dataSources: A locally managed Splunk Universal Forwarder scripted input reads `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/numastat` and `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` every 60 seconds, emitting one event per NUMA node to the deployment-selected `index=os` with the local convention `sourcetype=linux:numa_node_stats`. Required event fields are `numa_node`, `boot_id`, `numa_hit`, `numa_miss`, `numa_foreign`, `local_node`, and `other_node`; `_time` and `host` are Splunk metadata. This custom feed does not depend on the optional Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833).
app: Splunk Universal Forwarder native scripted input packaged in the locally managed `linux_numa_stats_input` app. The Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) is optional for other host telemetry and is not the source of this local source type or field contract.
spl:
index=os sourcetype="linux:numa_node_stats" earliest=-11m@m latest=@m
| fields _time host numa_node boot_id numa_hit numa_miss numa_foreign local_node other_node
| eval numa_node=tonumber(numa_node), boot_id=lower(boot_id), numa_hit=tonumber(numa_hit), numa_miss=tonumber(numa_miss), numa_foreign=tonumber(numa_foreign), local_node=tonumber(local_node), other_node=tonumber(other_node)
| where isnotnull(host) AND isnotnull(numa_node) AND numa_node>=0 AND match(boot_id,"^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$") AND numa_hit>=0 AND numa_miss>=0 AND numa_foreign>=0 AND local_node>=0 AND other_node>=0
| sort 0 host numa_node _time
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(_time) as previous_time last(boot_id) as previous_boot_id last(numa_hit) as previous_numa_hit last(numa_miss) as previous_numa_miss last(numa_foreign) as previous_numa_foreign last(local_node) as previous_local_node last(other_node) as previous_other_node by host numa_node
| eval interval_seconds=_time-previous_time, numa_hit_delta=numa_hit-previous_numa_hit, numa_miss_delta=numa_miss-previous_numa_miss, numa_foreign_delta=numa_foreign-previous_numa_foreign, local_node_delta=local_node-previous_local_node, other_node_delta=other_node-previous_other_node
| where boot_id=previous_boot_id AND interval_seconds>0 AND interval_seconds<=180 AND numa_hit_delta>=0 AND numa_miss_delta>=0 AND numa_foreign_delta>=0 AND local_node_delta>=0 AND other_node_delta>=0 AND _time>=relative_time(now(),"-10m@m")
| stats sum(numa_hit_delta) as numa_hit_pages sum(numa_miss_delta) as numa_miss_pages sum(numa_foreign_delta) as numa_foreign_pages sum(local_node_delta) as local_node_pages sum(other_node_delta) as other_node_pages sum(interval_seconds) as covered_seconds count as valid_intervals latest(_time) as _time by host numa_node
| eval hit_miss_pages=numa_hit_pages+numa_miss_pages, cpu_observed_allocation_pages=local_node_pages+other_node_pages
| where valid_intervals>=8 AND hit_miss_pages>=1000
| eval miss_pct=round(100*numa_miss_pages/hit_miss_pages,1), other_node_pct=if(cpu_observed_allocation_pages>0,round(100*other_node_pages/cpu_observed_allocation_pages,1),null()), sample_age_seconds=now()-_time
| where miss_pct>=10
| lookup linux_numa_exceptions.csv host numa_node OUTPUT valid_until_epoch change_id reason
| eval valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch), disposition=if(isnotnull(change_id) AND valid_until_epoch>=now(),"approved_test","investigate")
| table _time host numa_node numa_hit_pages numa_miss_pages hit_miss_pages miss_pct numa_foreign_pages local_node_pages other_node_pages other_node_pct valid_intervals covered_seconds sample_age_seconds disposition change_id reason
| sort 0 -miss_pct host numa_node
description: Reports a candidate Linux NUMA allocation imbalance when one host and memory node has at least eight valid counter intervals in the nominal ten-minute window, at least 1,000 newly allocated normal pages, and an allocation-policy miss ratio of 10% or more. Each row contains delta page counts, the miss percentage, collection coverage, sample age, and exception disposition; it does not equate a miss with measured remote-access latency.
value: Sustained allocation fallback can expose memory-policy, placement, or node-pressure problems before engineers spend time tuning an application blindly. Per-node deltas and preserved companion counters give platform teams a defensible starting point for correlating affected workloads and host memory conditions, while volume and completeness guards reduce pages caused by idle systems, reboot resets, or missing polls.
implementation: Deploy the exact `linux_numa_stats_input` collector at a 60-second interval, verify every custom field against the kernel sysfs files, and save the report on a five-minute schedule. Start with the local policy of at least 1,000 hit-plus-miss page increments, eight valid intervals, and `miss_pct>=10` over the nominal ten-minute window; baseline each hardware and workload class before paging, and alert only on `disposition=investigate`.
visualization: Use a latest-results table by host and NUMA node with miss percentage, hit and miss delta pages, hit-plus-miss pages, companion `other_node_pct`, valid intervals, covered seconds, sample age, disposition, and change ID. Add a 24-hour line chart of `miss_pct` by `host,numa_node` with a 10% policy line, plus separate collection-freshness and event-count panels for all expected nodes. Label all counter values as normal memory pages and the ratio as allocation-policy misses; do not label it remote-memory latency. Drill down to raw counter events and the process/locality runbook.

knownFalsePositives:
The counters are kernel observations, so a non-actionable result is usually an expected allocation policy or an unsuitable local threshold rather than fabricated telemetry.

1. **Authorized `numactl --interleave` or `mbind(2)` test** — A benchmark or placement test can intentionally allocate outside the CPU-local node and raise policy misses. Confirm the exact command, test owner, host, node, and approved UTC window; inspect the test process's `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps`. Add only that `host,numa_node` to `linux_numa_exceptions.csv` until the approved end time, while retaining the base-report row as `approved_test`.

2. **Kubernetes or systemd workload constrained by cpusets** — A container or service can have an allowed-memory-node set that differs from CPU placement, so the observed policy result can be expected for that deployment. Compare the workload's effective cpuset memory nodes and its process mappings with the node in the result. Correct placement or establish a reviewed host-class threshold; do not permanently suppress every Kubernetes node.

3. **PostgreSQL, Java, or analytics-worker startup** — A large process can allocate many pages during startup or worker fan-out and briefly exceed 10% before reaching steady state. Correlate the exact ten-minute interval with the named service start and compare the following two report runs. If startup behavior is accepted, use an exact-node, time-bound deployment exception rather than a recurring all-day filter.

4. **SAP HANA backup, database maintenance, or batch-memory surge** — Temporary pressure on an intended node can cause legitimate fallback while service remains within its tested objective. Compare per-node free memory and the application job record at the alert time, then confirm the miss ratio and pressure recover. Suppress only an approved job window; persistent recurrence requires capacity or placement review.

5. **Memoryless-node topology** — The Linux kernel documentation explicitly warns that `numa_hit`, `numa_miss`, and `numa_foreign` can be heavily skewed when nodes have CPUs but no memory. Compare `/sys/devices/system/node/has_cpu` with `has_normal_memory` before interpreting the row. Keep that topology out of the paging variant until an engineer defines and validates a suitable signal; document the exclusion rather than treating 10% as portable.

**Suppression contract:** `linux_numa_exceptions.csv` has headers `host,numa_node,valid_until_epoch,change_id,reason`, one active row per exact Splunk host and numeric node, no wildcards, and UTC epoch seconds in `valid_until_epoch`. Every row requires an accountable change ID and expires automatically. The base SPL classifies but never removes approved rows; only the alert variant appends `| where disposition="investigate"`.
reviewer: documentation-only review against Linux kernel, Red Hat, and Splunk primary sources; no runtime validation or SME sign-off
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and measurement boundary

Assign a Linux performance owner and a Splunk content owner. Use a Linux host on which `/sys/devices/system/node/node*/numastat` exists, and verify the intended nodes before deployment. The kernel defines these files as per-node hit/miss statistics in pages; huge pages have separate counters. `numa_hit` means allocation succeeded on the preferred node, while `numa_miss` is incremented on the node that satisfied an allocation intended for another node. The preferred node is often CPU-local, but memory policy can change it. Therefore this use case reports an allocation-policy miss ratio, not measured remote-memory latency or proof of application degradation.

Deploy a Splunk Universal Forwarder or another approved scripted-input execution tier. Create a local deployment app named `linux_numa_stats_input`; its name, `source=linux_numa_node_stats`, `sourcetype=linux:numa_node_stats`, and all emitted fields are local conventions. The optional Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) is not used by this collector. The forwarder account needs read access to the node `numastat` files and `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id`; test those reads as that account and do not add elevated privileges merely by assumption. Give the search role read access to the selected event index and permission to manage the report, alert, and lookup. This catalogue uses `index=os` as a deployment choice, so change the input, SPL, tests, and role together if another index is selected.

## 1. Configure the custom collector

Create `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_numa_stats_input/bin/numa_node_stats.sh` with mode `0755` and ownership appropriate to the forwarder service. Use this complete POSIX shell collector:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

boot_id=$(sed -n '1p' /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id)
case "$boot_id" in
  ????????-????-????-????-????????????) ;;
  *) exit 1 ;;
esac

found=0
for path in /sys/devices/system/node/node[0-9]*/numastat; do
    [ -r "$path" ] || continue
    found=1
    node_dir=${path%/numastat}
    node=${node_dir##*/node}
    awk -v node="$node" -v boot_id="$boot_id" '
      $1 == "numa_hit"     && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { hit=$2 }
      $1 == "numa_miss"    && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { miss=$2 }
      $1 == "numa_foreign" && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { foreign=$2 }
      $1 == "local_node"   && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { local=$2 }
      $1 == "other_node"   && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ { other=$2 }
      END {
        if (hit=="" || miss=="" || foreign=="" || local=="" || other=="") exit 1
        printf "numa_node=%s boot_id=%s numa_hit=%s numa_miss=%s numa_foreign=%s local_node=%s other_node=%s\n", node, boot_id, hit, miss, foreign, local, other
      }
    ' "$path"
done
[ "$found" -eq 1 ] || exit 1
```

The script reads the documented kernel interface directly and emits one `key=value` line per readable node. It does not parse the column layout of the human-facing `numastat` command, invent a socket identifier, or require the `numactl` package. `boot_id` lets the search reject counter transitions across a reboot. Configure `$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_numa_stats_input/local/inputs.conf`:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/linux_numa_stats_input/bin/numa_node_stats.sh]
disabled = 0
interval = 60
index = os
source = linux_numa_node_stats
sourcetype = linux:numa_node_stats
```

Splunk documents that scripted inputs run the command at the configured interval and index its standard output, with the next invocation scheduled relative to completion. A continuously connected host with two NUMA nodes therefore produces approximately 2,880 small events per day, not a guaranteed exact count. On the parsing tier set `SHOULD_LINEMERGE=false` and use collection time because the source line has no timestamp; on the search tier enable automatic `key=value` extraction:

```ini
[linux:numa_node_stats]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
DATETIME_CONFIG = CURRENT
KV_MODE = auto
```

Place each setting on the correct tier for the deployment topology. Restart the affected forwarder after changing `inputs.conf`. No inbound port, API credential, HEC token, premium app, modular input, or CIM acceleration is required.

## 2. Verify source semantics and field quality

Run the script as the forwarder account. It must print one line for each readable `nodeN/numastat` file, with the same node number and five nonnegative counter values. Compare each emitted line immediately with its source file; these cumulative values can change under workload, so do not compare samples taken minutes apart. Run `splunk btool inputs list --debug` on a representative forwarder and confirm the winning script path, 60-second interval, `index=os`, source, source type, and enabled state.

Search `index=os sourcetype="linux:numa_node_stats" earliest=-5m | table _time host numa_node boot_id numa_hit numa_miss numa_foreign local_node other_node`. Expect roughly five events per continuously collected node, one stable boot UUID, numeric counters that never decrease within that boot, and no missing fields. Compare the set of `numa_node` values with `/sys/devices/system/node/online`. Also compare `/sys/devices/system/node/has_cpu` and `has_normal_memory`; if they identify memoryless nodes, do not enable this alert until an engineer qualifies the topology because the kernel documents potentially heavy skew.

The fields are not CIM-normalized, and no `cimSpl` is asserted. Do not map `numa_miss` to a latency, byte, event, or process field. All five values count normal pages. `numa_foreign` is useful as the counterpart on the node from which allocation was intended; `local_node` and `other_node` describe allocations according to the CPU node. They are retained for triage, but only `numa_miss/(numa_hit+numa_miss)` drives this report.

## 3. Save and understand the search

Save the catalogue SPL as `linux_numa_allocation_miss_ratio` and schedule it every five minutes. The explicit `earliest=-11m@m latest=@m` obtains one baseline minute plus the nominal ten-minute evaluation period and avoids the incomplete current minute. `sort` orders every host and node, and `streamstats current=f window=1` attaches the preceding sample. The search subtracts cumulative counters only when the boot UUID is unchanged, all deltas are nonnegative, and adjacent samples are no more than 180 seconds apart. It then keeps current samples in the last ten complete minutes and aggregates delta pages separately for every `host,numa_node`.

A row is eligible only with at least eight valid intervals and at least 1,000 hit-plus-miss page increments (`numa_hit_pages+numa_miss_pages`). These completeness and volume floors prevent a tiny idle-node denominator or sparse collection from becoming an operational page. The inclusive `miss_pct>=10` condition means `numa_miss_pages` is at least 10 percent of the hit-plus-miss denominator for that node. Ten percent, 1,000 pages, eight intervals, the 60-second poll, and the nominal ten-minute window are local starting policies—not Linux, Red Hat, or Splunk defaults. Baseline each hardware model, kernel line, memory policy, and workload class; record approved tuning with the owner and effective date.

Create `linux_numa_exceptions.csv` with headers `host,numa_node,valid_until_epoch,change_id,reason`. Require an exact Splunk host and numeric node, UTC epoch seconds, a bounded expiry, and an accountable change identifier. The base report must retain both dispositions. Save `linux_numa_allocation_miss_alert` from the report, append `| where disposition="investigate"`, and trigger when result count is greater than zero. Deduplicate notifications by `host,numa_node` for one schedule interval, then notify again while the condition persists according to local incident policy; do not use an indefinite throttle.

## 4. Validate the logic without overstating execution

Execute the positive and negative scenarios in an isolated index or equivalent fixture, substituting only the index name. For `numa-positive`, the eight deltas total 7,200 hits and 800 misses, so the report must calculate an 8,000-page hit-plus-miss denominator and exactly 10.0 percent. Verify both lookup paths: absent or expired lookup data yields `investigate`; an active exact-key row yields `approved_test` in the base report and no output in the alert-only variant. For `numa-negative`, eight increments of 951 hits and 49 misses total 4.9 percent and must not return a row.

Test the guards separately. A boot-ID change, decreasing counter, interval over 180 seconds, malformed UUID, null field, fewer than eight valid intervals, or fewer than 1,000 hit-plus-miss page increments must not create an alert row. Confirm that the freshness panel shows missing data so rejected or absent samples are not represented as healthy locality. This documentation review verifies the source definitions and expected arithmetic only; it did not run the collector or SPL on a production host. A later runtime reviewer should retain script output, raw events, search job IDs, expected calculations, and the tested Splunk and kernel versions.

For host acceptance, run an owner-approved lab workload whose memory policy and placement are known. Capture `/sys/devices/system/node/nodeN/numastat` immediately before and after the interval, then compare those counter changes with the indexed deltas. Use `numastat` for a human-readable cross-check when the package is available and inspect `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps` for the test process's policy and per-node mapping. Do not deliberately exhaust node memory or change production binding merely to make this alert fire.

## 5. Operationalize, investigate, and troubleshoot

Build the latest-results, trend, and freshness panels described in `visualization`. Restrict lookup editing to the operations role that owns approved tests; dashboard readers need no write access. On an `investigate` result, first verify the latest raw event against the node sysfs file and check whether the host rebooted, a node changed state, or collection was delayed. Then identify workloads active in the same ten-minute interval. For a candidate process, inspect its approved service/container configuration and `/proc/<pid>/numa_maps`; compare CPU and memory constraints, memory policy, application startup, and per-node free memory. Treat the ratio as a symptom. Rebinding CPUs or memory, changing cpusets, enabling interleave, migrating pages, or adding memory can alter behavior and must follow application and capacity review rather than being an automatic alert action.

If no events arrive, execute the collector as the forwarder user, verify the sysfs glob and boot-ID file are visible in that service's mount namespace, inspect the effective scripted-input stanza, and look in `splunkd.log` for errors associated with the exact script path and scripted-input execution. A non-NUMA kernel or guest may legitimately expose no matching node files; exclude it from the expected-host inventory instead of installing an empty alert.

If raw lines exist but fields are null, confirm the exact `linux:numa_node_stats` spelling and that `KV_MODE=auto` is active on the search tier. If a poll becomes one merged event, check `SHOULD_LINEMERGE=false` where parsing occurs. If multiple events for the same node share a minute, use `source`, `host`, and forwarder configuration to find duplicate input stanzas and keep one collector. If all rows disappear, check the freshness and guard fields before declaring recovery: a reboot, negative delta, long gap, low volume, or insufficient interval count is deliberately excluded. If ratios differ from manual arithmetic, compare deltas rather than lifetime counter values and confirm the denominator is `numa_hit_pages+numa_miss_pages`, not `local_node_pages+other_node_pages`. Memoryless nodes, huge-page behavior, and application latency remain outside this alert's interpretation.
grandmaExplanation: We watch whether a many-processor server repeatedly puts newly requested memory somewhere other than the preferred place. That warning helps the team investigate placement or capacity before changing the application blindly.
